records.title: EW RSS 008 - Using plate compactor for compaction earth works beside retaining wall
records.notes:
Plate compactor is only effective for thin layers (100–150 mm). It provides lower compaction energy compared to roller compactors. Compaction may only be achieved at the surface, resulting in inconsistent density. Plate compactor is mainly suitable for confined areas and narrow spaces near structures.
 
 A plate compactor is not suitable for achieving 95% compaction in 300 mm thick backfill layers due to its limited compaction depth.

 Insufficient filtration of backfill material
 Soil migration and clogging of the weep hole
 Ineffective drainage behind the retaining wall
 Increased hydrostatic pressure on the wall
 Potential long-term structural issues

records.refNo: MBW RSS 001 - MLT commencement without proper planning and approved documentation
records.title:
During a site surveillance at BTP-F, it was observed that the Contractor carried out the Maintained Load Test (MLT) for Test Pile TP3 without proper planning and without the timely submission and approval of the required documents. Among the observations are as follows, but not limited to:
 
 
  1) The work was carried out on 12 July 2026 without proper work planning and with only last-minute notification to the Consultant. 
 
 2) The work commenced without an approved Method Statement (MOS) for reference by the Site team and the Consultant. 
 
 3) The General Contractor (GC) arranged the kentledge without an approved design drawing endorsed by a Professional Engineer (PE). 
 
 4) As there was no approved MOS or approved kentledge design for reference, the GC proceeded with the first cycle of the MLT without installing the complete kentledge loading system. Based on the records, only 290 tonnes of kentledge had been installed for the first cycle. The remaining kentledge of 590 tonnes for second 2 cycle, was only installed after the first cycle was completed at 2:00 p.m. on 13 July 2026. The second cycle then commenced at 8:00 p.m. on 13 July 2026.
 
  5) At the start of the second cycle, the loading sequence could only can commenced at 100% of the working load instead of start at 25% working load. There is a possibility that ground settlement occurred during the installation and arrangement of the additional kentledge for the second cycle, which may aAected the loading sequence and validity of the test results.

records.refNo: MBW RSS 002 - Piling Work Started Without Approved MOS & Setting-Out Plan
records.title:
During the site inspection, it was observed that the GC had commenced piling works at site without obtaining the necessary approval for the Piling Method Statement (MOS) and Piling Setting-Out Shop Drawing. The piling activities were started prior to the completion of the required document review and approval process. This is not in accordance with the project quality control and inspection requirements. Concern & Risk 
 Commencing piling works without approved documents may result in: 
 1. Risk of incorrect pile location, alignment, spacing, or setting-out. 
 2. Difficulty in verifying the works against the approved design during inspection.
 3. Potential rework and additional costs if discrepancies are identified after piling works have commenced.
  4. Incomplete or difficult-to-close quality records and inspection documentation. The test shall be deemed as REJECTED, until all of the above has been properly addressed and in placed.

records.refNo: MBW RSS 003 - Short penetration piles and conduct PDA testing for Block F.
records.title:
During site surveillance and review of the piling records for Block F, it was observed that several installed piles exhibit short penetration lengths relative to the design specifications. 

The Contractor is hereby reminded to carry out re-tapping on these short penetration piles and perform Pile Driving Analyzer (PDA) testing strictly in accordance with the approved Third Batch Pile Selection and pile group proposals (refer to the attached block layout and schedule). Furthermore, test results must be submitted promptly upon completion to determine any additional pile requirements. 
 Further Implications 
Without immediate action to address this issue, potential consequences include:  

•	a) Structural safety risks, including uncertain load-bearing capacity and potential settlement issues for foundation elements resting on insufficient pile penetration depths.
•	b) Non-compliance with approved structural design standards, leading to potential rejections or delays in engineering verification.
•	c) Subsequent project schedule delays due to late submission of PDA test results, pending additional pile proposals, and deferred substructure works.

Note: Any subsequent structural or substructure works proceeding without fulfilling these PDA testing requirements and rectifying the short penetration piles shall NOT BE ALLOWED.

records.refNo: MBW RSS 004 - Pile cut-off and excavation works without submitting the pile eccentricity report.
records.title:
During routine site surveillance, it was observed that the Contractor(CCYR) has proceeded with pile cut-off and excavation works for the pile caps without first submitting and obtaining approval for the pile eccentricity report. 
Proceeding with pile cut-off prior to proper surveying, recording, and assessment of pile deviations compromises the foundation's structural integrity tracking and quality assurance workflow. 
Further Implications 
Without addressing this issue, potential consequences include: 

•        a) Risk of undetected pile out-of-tolerance (eccentricity) conditions being permanently hidden after cut-off works, leading to severe structural non-compliance.
•        b) Potential abortive work, costly redesigns, or the need for expensive remedial measures (such as adding extra piles or enlarging pile caps) if excessive eccentricities are discovered after the fact.
•        c) Project delays and disputes regarding liability for unauthorized works carried out ahead of mandatory engineering submissions and verifications.
Note: Any subsequent structural work (including blinding concrete, rebar installation, or concreting) to proceed without official review and approval of the pile eccentricity report
shall NOT BE ALLOWED.

Based on the review of the submitted as-built survey drawing for piling works at Gridline 22-33/A-G, it was observed that several piles exhibit out-of-tolerance pile eccentricities. 
Proceeding with subsequent structural works without formal structural assessment, disposition, and remedial design approval for these eccentric piles compromises the foundation's structural integrity and does not comply with project quality assurance workflows. 
Further Implications 

a) 	Risk of unverified load distributions and structural non-compliance resulting from eccentric column/pile cap loading. 
b) 	Potential abortive work, costly redesigns, or the necessity for major structural remedial measures (such as adding anchor/correction piles or enlarging pile caps) if not rectified prior to cap construction. 
c) 	Project delays and contractual disputes regarding liability and unauthorized continuation of works over non-compliant foundations. 
Note: Any subsequent work on affected pile caps without approved eccentricity disposition shall NOT BE ALLOWED.
